mask.title: Detector Mask
mask.circularTooltip:
Apply a circular mask to the detector pattern.

EDAX-style files (.h5): patterns are stored with a circular
detector aperture — the corners are black in the raw data.
Enabling the mask improves auto-contrast range, removes the
dynamic-BG halo at the disc edge, and helps NCC during indexing.

Oxford H5OINA files: the full rectangular camera frame is stored —
a circular mask would DISCARD real diffraction data. Keep OFF.

Auto-enabled for EDAX, auto-disabled for Oxford on file load;
manual toggle is honoured until the next file load.
mask.radiusTooltip:
Mask radius as percent of the inscribed circle.
100% = exactly tangent to the shorter detector edge.
Lower values exclude more of the dark edge bleed.

processing.title: Pattern Processing
processing.bgDynamicTooltip:
Remove background using dynamic method (per-pattern Gaussian blur).
Best for most EBSD patterns. (Alt+D)
processing.bgStaticTooltip:
Remove background using static background image.
Requires a static background stored in the HDF5 file. (Alt+S)
processing.windowSizeTooltip:
Kernel window size for pattern processing filters.
Larger values smooth more but may blur fine details.
processing.frameAverageTooltip: Average neighboring patterns to reduce noise. (Alt+A)
processing.autoContrastTooltip:
Automatically stretch pattern contrast to full dynamic range. (Alt+C)
With Circular Mask enabled, percentiles are computed from inside the disc only.
processing.claheTooltipTitle: CLAHE — Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization
processing.claheTooltipP1: Divides the pattern into a grid of kernel × kernel tiles, equalises each tile's histogram independently, then blends the tiles smoothly. Limits how much any single tile can be amplified (the "contrast limit") so noise doesn't explode.
processing.claheTooltipP2: On raw EBSD: faint Kikuchi bands in the dark detector edges become as visible as the bright central ones. Drives the Method B symmetry NCC from ~0.15 → ~0.5 on real patterns.
processing.claheTooltipChoose1: 4–6: aggressive local contrast, amplifies fine band detail — but also noise. Use on clean, well-exposed patterns.
processing.claheTooltipChoose2: 8 (default): kikuchipy convention, ≈ ⅛ of a 118 px pattern. Good balance for most data.
processing.claheTooltipChoose3: 12–16: smoother result, behaves more like global contrast stretching. Good for noisy patterns where small kernels make the speckle worse than the bands.
processing.claheTooltipChoose4: 24+: barely adaptive — comparable to a plain histogram stretch. Rarely useful.
processing.claheTooltipRule: Rule of thumb: kernel ≈ pattern_width / 12. For 60 px patterns try 5–6; for 256 px try 16.
processing.recommendedPipelineTooltipP1: Runs three preprocessing steps in one click — kikuchipy's recommended sequence for raw EBSD patterns:
processing.recommendedPipelineTooltipStep1: Static BG removal — subtracts the scan-average background (removes detector blemishes + non-uniform illumination).
processing.recommendedPipelineTooltipStep2: Dynamic BG removal — subtracts a per-pattern low-pass-filtered version (removes the radial intensity falloff specific to each pattern).
processing.recommendedPipelineTooltipStep3: CLAHE — local-contrast enhances band visibility using the kernel size set above.
processing.recommendedPipelineTooltipNote: Uses the current Circular Mask + CLAHE kernel settings. Operates on the currently-selected dataset; result becomes the active one.
processing.brightnessTooltip:
Client-side brightness for pattern display (100 = neutral, 1.0x).
Applied as CSS filter: brightness(value/100) — a linear scale, not true gamma correction.
For true gamma (non-linear tone curve), use the Filter dropdown or export + process externally.
processing.filterTooltip:
Filter for pattern visualization.
Sobel: gradient-based edges. Canny: threshold-based edges.
FFT Highpass: removes low-frequency background.
CLAHE: local contrast enhancement.
processing.interpTooltip:
Pattern display interpolation method.
nearest: pixel-accurate, no smoothing (default).
bilinear/bicubic: smooth display for publication quality.
lanczos: highest quality, best for zoomed-in viewing.
processing.batchAutoContrastTooltip:
Apply auto-contrast normalization to all patterns in the dataset.
Stretches each pattern's histogram to use the full dynamic range.
processing.batchConfirmMessage: Apply auto-contrast to ALL patterns? This may take a while for large datasets.
processing.exportPatternTooltip:
Save the current pattern as PNG or TIFF image file.
Exports the pattern as displayed (with current filter and brightness).
processing.resetProcessingTooltip: Reset brightness, filter, and interpolation to defaults
processing.compareDatasetsTooltip: Open side-by-side comparison of two datasets at the same pixel. (Ctrl+K)
